title: Netflix Premieres 'Who Killed the Banker’s Widow?' on December 4
summary: Netflix announces that Who Killed the Banker’s Widow?, a new documentary retracing the murder of María del Carmen Martínez, widow of the former president of Caja de Ahorros del Mediterráneo (CAM), will premiere on December 4.

Netflix announces that


Who Killed the Banker’s Widow?,


a new documentary retracing the murder of María del Carmen Martínez, widow of the former president of Caja de Ahorros del Mediterráneo (CAM), will premiere on


December 4


. Nearly a decade later, the crime remains shrouded in mystery.


The documentary revisits a murder that shook one of Spain’s wealthiest families and brought to light a complex web of family disputes, secrets and financial interests. Through the investigation conducted by journalists


Braulio García Jaén and Bárbara Ayuso


, creators of the


El enemigo


podcast for EL PAÍS Audio, the production retraces the events, examines conflicting accounts and explores the contradictions and unanswered questions that shaped the police and judicial investigations.


Produced by


LACOproductora, part of PRISA Media


, and directed by


Maxi González


(


En primicia


), the documentary draws on the journalists’ work, with both also contributing to the narration. It features a range of testimonies and explores new investigative leads uncovered by the journalists, offering other perspective on the case. An investigation that goes beyond the crime itself to challenge the assumptions surrounding it and delve deeper into a search for the truth that, nearly a decade later, remains ongoing.


Synopsis:


When a prominent banker dies, his wife inherits the powerful golden share, granting her control over key decisions within the family business empire. Five years later, the widow is found murdered, shot twice in the head, while collecting her Porsche from the dealership run by her son-in-law.


The crime exposes deep-rooted rivalries within the company’s leadership, a family divided into two opposing camps, and one unanswered question: Who killed the banker’s wife?


About LACOproductora:


LACOproductora is the audiovisual production company of PRISA Media. Focused on film and television production, it develops factual and entertainment programmes, true crime productions, fiction films and documentaries. Its releases include large-scale entertainment shows such as


That’s My Jam


(La 1), personality-driven programmes such as


Mis raíces


(Cuatro), and documentary series such as


En primicia


(La 2). The company has also presented


Flores para Antonio


in the Official Selection of the San Sebastián International Film Festival. The documentary was the most-watched film in Spanish cinemas in 2025, received a Forqué Award and an In-Edit Award, and was nominated for Best Documentary Film at the Goya Awards, winning in the Best Original Song category.
